name: concept-resolution
purpose: Doc-17 pre-registered corpus for the embedding+adjudicator concept-resolution test (nmemo-uhp.19). 12 canonical memory/lifetime/concurrency mechanisms in 6 hard near-miss sibling pairs. Each mechanism has a NEUTRAL behavioural spec (the ground-truth pivot that fixes which mechanism it is) written to avoid dictating register vocabulary. Three prose REGISTERS per mechanism (normative/advisory/reference) are authored at run time by three INDEPENDENT blind Haiku calls that never see each other's output and are never told this is a matching test — so any vocabulary gap arises from independent authorship, not from me.

registers.normative: Formal standards / rule language: state what a program 'shall not' do and why it is a correctness or safety hazard. Use your register's natural vocabulary; do NOT quote the specification text you are given.
registers.advisory: Practitioner guideline language: advise what to prefer and what to avoid in day-to-day coding, in terms of idioms and habits. Use your register's natural vocabulary; do NOT quote the specification text you are given.
registers.reference: Reference-manual / textbook language: describe neutrally how the underlying language mechanism behaves and what its semantics are. Use your register's natural vocabulary; do NOT quote the specification text you are given.

mechanisms.spec: Storage for data is obtained while the program runs, for an amount that need not be known in advance, and the program must later return that storage explicitly.
Storage for data comes into being automatically when a region of code is entered and is reclaimed automatically the instant that region is left.
A single block of previously-obtained storage is given back to the system on two separate occasions.
A block of storage is accessed for reading or writing after it has already been given back to the system.
A handle continues to be followed even though the storage it designates has already ceased to exist.
A handle that currently designates nothing is followed as though it designated valid storage.
Storage obtained for a group of items is given back using the single-item form of the release operation, or the reverse.
Storage obtained through one management facility is given back through a different, incompatible management facility.
Responsibility for releasing a resource passes across an interface boundary without it being made clear which side is obliged to release it.
Several independent parts of a program jointly hold one resource, and it is released only after the last of them has finished using it.
A program acquires exclusive access to a shared region but, on at least one path of execution, leaves without giving that access back.
A program retains exclusive access to a shared region while performing a lengthy or waiting operation that does not require that access to be held.
